Hon'Ble Mrs Justice P. Sree Sudha
Oral Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the claimants against the judgment and award dated 06.11.2023 passed by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and J.M.F.C., Bidar [for short NC: 2025:KHC-K:6786 HC-KAR 'Tribunal'], in MVC No.364/2022, seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and J.M.F.C., Bidar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. One Mumtaz, aged 56 years met with an accident on 14.06.2021 and died.
Her children filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.20,50,000/- with interest.
The Tribunal considered the entire materials on record and granted Rs.12,52,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
Aggrieved by the said order, claimants filed this appeal.
3. Heard arguments of both the parties and perused the materials available on record.

Sirajuddin And Ors vs Khadeer Pasha And Anr on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29104033/
2 4.

entities.text: Sirajuddin And Ors vs Khadeer Pasha And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The main contentions of the claimants are that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by doing Coolie work, but the Tribunal without any basis assessed the same at Rs.12,000/- per month.
It is further stated that the Tribunal is not justified in not considering 10% future prospects.
Therefore, they pray for enhancement of the compensation.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6786 HC-KAR 5.

The learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company contended that claimants are major sons of the deceased and not dependent on the income of the deceased and thus, they are not entitled for any compensation.
6. Admittedly, the claimants are children of the deceased.
They have lost their mother in the accident and their father is pre-deceased.
Therefore, argument of the learned counsel for respondent-Insurance Company that the claimants are not dependent on the income of the deceased cannot be accepted.
7. The deceased was aged 56 years at the time of accident.
Though it is stated that she was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, no document is produced to prove the same.

In the absence of proof of income, as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, this Court finds it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.14,250/- per month for the accident of the year 2021, instead of NC: 2025:KHC-K:6786 HC-KAR Rs.12,000/-.
As per the principal of law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance CO. Ltd vs. Pranay Sethi and Others1 10% of income is to be awarded towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance CO. Ltd vs. Pranay Sethi and Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, 10% of Rs.14,250/- comes to Rs.1,425/-, thus, total income of the deceased comes to Rs.15,675/-.
If 1/3rd of this amount is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased, the claimants entitled for 2/3rd of the income.

Thus, the loss of dependency comes as under:
Rs.15,675/- x 12 x 9 x 2/3 = Rs.11,26,600/-.
8.
The claimants being children of the deceased are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of parental consortium, in total Rs.1,20,000/-.

9. The claimants are also entitled for an amount of Rs.30,000/- under the conventional heads as per the 2017 ACJ 2700 SC NC: 2025:KHC-K:6786 HC-KAR citation in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. Accordingly, the claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.12,78,600/- as against Rs.12,52,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
There will be enhancement of Rs.26,600/-.
11. Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company has already deposited the amount awarded by the Tribunal.

12. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
Sirajuddin And Ors vs Khadeer Pasha And Anr on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29104033/
3 ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed.
(ii) The appellants are entitled for compensation of Rs.26,600/- with interest at 6%
per annum from the date of petition till realization in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

entities.text: Sirajuddin And Ors vs Khadeer Pasha And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: NC: 2025:KHC-K:6786 HC-KAR (iii) Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount along with interest within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, the claimants are permitted to withdraw the entire enhanced compensation with interest equally.
